YA-MS aiuta a prevedere e a seguire in d: YA-MS helps you forecast and follow live the meteor scatter conditions between your station and a DX station, from 28 to 432 MHz. For each active meteor shower it tells you how much the position of its radiant favours your path (the efficiency), at what times, from which side of the path the reflections arrive and where it is best to point the antenna. Alongside the forecast it shows data measured live: the counts of the Collm meteor radar, the cameras of the Global Meteor Network, the CMOR radar, the GRAVES transmitter and the meteor scatter traffic collected from the clusters and from PSKReporter.
Il programma è gratuito, funziona su Win: The program is free, runs on Windows, Linux (including Raspberry Pi) and macOS, and is translated into 36 languages. It does not control the radio or the rotator: for the contact you use your usual digital-mode program (MSHV, WSJT-X).
Il manuale descrive le linguette una per: The manual describes the tabs one by one, starting from the forecast calculation. Each chapter tells you what the tab shows, what each control does and how to read the results. Chapter 14 collects the most common procedures, chapter 15 the frequent problems. How the efficiency is calculated, with sources and checks, is explained in the document "Explanation of the efficiency calculation"; the complete equations are in the Calculation Manual (doc folder).
informazione utile per capire o usare me: useful information for understanding or making better use of a function.
errore frequente, limite del calcolo o c: common mistake, limit of the calculation or behaviour worth knowing.

Il mio locator e quota m: il tuo locator: My locator and height m: your Maidenhead locator (4, 6 or 8 characters; the centre of the square is used) and the height of the station above sea level.
Corrispondente e quota m: locator e quot: DX station and height m: locator and height of the station to be worked.
Banda MHz: 28, 50, 70, 144, 222 o 432 MH: Band MHz: 28, 50, 70, 144, 222 or 432 MHz. It is used for the antenna gain and lobe, for the path loss and the link budget, and for the flux estimate.
Calcola: ricalcola la tratta (campioname: Calculate: recalculates the path (sampling of the E layer, less than a second).
Antenna az: azimut dell'antenna, sempre: Antenna az: antenna azimuth, always towards the DX station.
Quota scie km e dal radar: quota delle s: Trail height km and from radar: height of the meteor trails. With "from radar" ticked, the most frequent height measured by the Collm radar is used (usually 88-90 km); untick it to type it in manually.
Elevazione lobo °: elevazione del massim: Lobe elevation °: elevation of the maximum of your antenna's vertical lobe. A beam fixed at 0° still has its main lobe a few degrees above the horizon, because of the ground reflection: usually 3-8°, depending on the antenna height in wavelengths.
diagramma d'antenna: accesa (di partenza: antenna pattern: when on (default), the reflection points count with the vertical gain of the two antennas: full around the maximum of the lobe, less and less towards the horizon and upwards. When off, the lobe elevation is a hard limit: points seen lower down do not count.
Antenna Yagi: boom m: lunghezza del boom: Yagi antenna: boom m: length of the boom. Next to it the program writes the length in wavelengths, the gain (DL6WU curve) and the horizontal and vertical -3 dB beamwidth. Below 2 λ the estimate is not very accurate.
Hot spot dal punto medio km e auto (AMS): Hot spot from midpoint km and auto (AMS): distance of Hot A and Hot B from the midpoint. With "auto (AMS)" ticked it follows J. Richardson's table quoted by DJ5HG (13° offset at 1000 km, 10° beyond 1500 km); untick it to type 30-400 km manually (MSHV uses 150 km).
Con \"diagramma d'antenna\" spento e il: With "antenna pattern" off and the lobe at a few degrees, on a long path the two stations may not see any common point of the layer: all efficiencies are 0 and the warning "NO COMMON ZONE" appears, with the lobe or trail height that would be needed. Example: JN70CN - JO76QP, 1791 km, lobe at 3°, trails at 88.5 km.
Data del calcolo (UTC): il giorno del ca: Calculation date (UTC): the day of the calculation. It applies to Forecast calculation, to the 24-hour table of Efficiency calculation and to the timeline of GRAVES radar. By default it is today, and at midnight it moves on to the new day.
Ore (da −12 a +36 h): sposta il momento: Hours (−12 to +36 h): shifts the moment of the calculation, in 15-minute steps. Next to it: "Calculation for: now" or the chosen date and time.
Real time: returns to the current moment.
1) Scrivi Il mio locator e la quota. 2): 1) Enter My locator and the height. 2) Enter the locator and height of the DX station, or click on the map of Forecast calculation: left click = DX station, right click = your station. 3) Choose the band. 4) Enter the boom length and the lobe elevation of your antenna. 5) Press Calculate: the status bar confirms "Path computed: ... km, ... reflection points sampled".
Le impostazioni vengono salvate in data/: The settings are saved in data/config.ini on closing and at every calculation: at the next start you will find the same path.
La prima sotto-linguetta del gruppo Calc: The first sub-tab of the Forecast calculation group shows on one screen where the useful trails are falling right now and where to point. Everything refers to the moment chosen with the date and the hours slider.
Sopra la mappa una striscia riassume il: Above the map a strip summarises the calculation for that moment: date and time, path index (sum of ZHR × efficiency of the active showers), the most useful shower with its ZHR and its efficiency (also in dB relative to DJ5HG's reference), the number of showers above the horizon and the recommended Hot with its azimuth.
A sinistra la mappa d'Europa vista dall': On the left, the map of Europe seen from above (east to the right), with the degree scale all around:
linea verde: la tratta vera tra i due lo: green line: the true path between the two locators;
Hot A e Hot B: i due hot spot ai lati de: Hot A and Hot B: the two hot spots on either side of the midpoint. Red = recommended, pink = outside the antenna lobe, grey = already inside the lobe (with a warning);
lobo dell'antenna: il settore a -3 dB at: antenna lobe: the -3 dB sector around the antenna azimuth;
Limite A e Limite B, tenui: i bordi più: Limit A and Limit B, faint: the farthest edges of the sky seen by both stations, not points to aim at;
linea gialla: la direzione in cui lo sci: yellow line: the direction in which the selected shower (or the most favourable one) sweeps the sky; orange dots: the two perpendicular pointings (radiant azimuth ±90°);
zone PREV, ellissi chiare: dove cadono a: PREV zones, light ellipses: where the most probable trails are falling right now, one for each side of the path.
Clic sinistro sulla mappa = locator del: Left click on the map = locator of the DX station, right click = locator of your station; the path is recalculated immediately. The legend is a collapsible column to the right of the map. The checkboxes above the shower list turn on and off the Hot directions, the map of Europe and the top view.
Per ogni sciame: nome e sigla IMO, ZHR i: For each shower: name and IMO code, ZHR at this moment, azimuth and elevation of the radiant from your station, efficiency for the path, prevailing side (A or B), best pointing, rise and set of the radiant. Clicking a row selects the shower: the yellow line and the orange dots follow it.
5.4 La piccola volta celeste e il testo: 5.4 The small sky dome and the calculation text
I radianti visti dalla tua stazione, con: The radiants seen from your station, with the IMO code and the daily track in cyan. Yellow = efficiency at least 50 % and ZHR at least 2; orange = at least 20 %; dark red = less; grey = almost inactive. The orange line through the zenith gives the right antenna directions, orthogonal to the shower's motion. Next to it, the calculation text: path, midpoint, recommended Hot with the percentage of expected reflections, limits of the common zone.
In basso a destra le scie più probabili: At the bottom right, the most probable trails as seen from the antenna towards the DX station: horizontally the azimuth relative to the DX station (A on the left, B on the right), vertically the elevation. Each trail is a segment oriented towards the radiant, thicker the more probable it is. The antenna lobe, the DX station and the Hots are also drawn.

RADIANTE TROPPO ALTO: un radiante utile: RADIANT TOO HIGH: a useful radiant is above 70°; the trails fall almost vertically and reflect little towards the path.

NESSUNA ZONA COMUNE: nessun punto dello: NO COMMON ZONE: no point of the layer is visible from both stations; the warning tells you by how much it falls short and what would be needed.
Un resoconto testuale della tratta, sele: A text report of the path, which can be selected and copied, and on the right the chart of the antenna elevation as a function of the distance to the reflection point, for three trail heights.
Potenza W (400), Guadagno antenna dBi (1: Power W (400), Antenna gain dBi (14; same antenna at both ends), Minimum signal dBm (-130), Trail density q = 10^14 electrons/m: they are used for the link budget.
Raggio iniziale della scia: doppio dell': Initial trail radius: twice the ITU value (Stober 2021, cautious, default), ITU-R P.843, or excluded. The larger the radius, the more is lost at the higher frequencies.
Durata dei ping tra le bande: teorica λ²: Ping duration between bands: theoretical λ² (McKinley, SM6FHZ; cautious, default) or observed (HamSCI MSQP measurements by NN4SA, Perseids 2026: from 50 to 144 MHz the pings get 1.5 times shorter instead of 8).
GEOMETRIA DELLA TRATTA: stazioni e quote: PATH GEOMETRY: stations and heights, distance, azimuth, midpoint, trail height, antenna elevation towards the midpoint.
HOT A / HOT B: locator, azimut, scarto d: HOT A / HOT B: locator, azimuth, offset from the direct bearing, distance and elevation of each hot spot.
LIMITI DELLA ZONA COMUNE: portata alla q: COMMON ZONE LIMITS: range at trail height up to the horizon, the antenna lobe with its maximum and its vertical width, Limit A and Limit B; gain and lobe of the Yagi.
ATTENUAZIONE DI TRATTA: per punto medio,: PATH LOSS: for the midpoint, Hot A and Hot B, at 28, 50, 70, 144, 222 and 432 MHz (trail crossing the plane of the path, the least favourable case).
BILANCIO: potenza ed EIRP, attenuazione,: LINK BUDGET: power and EIRP, path loss, signal at the antenna, minimum signal and margin; the best case (trail in the plane of the path) and the margin with OH5IY's average path loss.
REGOLE SPERIMENTALI TRA LE BANDE: numero: EXPERIMENTAL RULES BETWEEN BANDS: number, strength and duration of the reflections relative to 144 MHz; IARU maximum ping; duration observed from the MSQP measurements.
Un margine positivo dice che una scia so: A positive margin means that an average underdense trail is enough to close the path with your station; a negative margin means that denser trails or overdense meteors are needed. It is an estimate: the reference remains on-air experience.
L'efficienza dice, in percentuale, quant: The efficiency tells you, as a percentage, how much the position of a shower's radiant allows reflections on your path: 100 % is the most favourable position for that path. This sub-tab shows it hour by hour for the day of the "Calculation date", with the values at the middle of each hour.
ORA MIGLIORE DEL GIORNO: l'ora con l'ind: BEST TIME OF THE DAY: the hour with the highest path index and the prevailing side.
SCIAME PIÙ FAVOREVOLE: lo sciame che con: MOST FAVOURABLE SHOWER: the shower that contributes the most, with the hour, the side and the two best pointings.
ADESSO: indice e lato in questa ora e l': NOW: index and side in this hour and the recommended Hot (only if the chosen day is today).
PREVISIONE SPERIMENTALE: riflessioni all: EXPERIMENTAL FORECAST: reflections per hour expected now, in 1 hour and in 2 hours (chapter 8).
Quando un riquadro non ha valori dice pe: When a box has no values it tells you why: no common zone, no active shower, or unfavourable radiants for the whole day. The tooltip of each box explains what it shows. Below the boxes, when needed, the NO COMMON ZONE warning and a band explaining the letters A and B.
Prudente (di partenza): quota delle scie: Cautious (default): trail height from radar, normal trails, angle β on. It gives the lowest values.
Come DJ5HG: quota fissa di 102 km, scie: As DJ5HG: fixed height of 102 km, longer trails with a low radiant, angle β on; it mirrors the QTFGUI program.
Personalizzata: si seleziona da sola qua: Custom: selected automatically when you manually change one of the checkboxes or the height.
Scie più lunghe con il radiante basso (D: Longer trails with a low radiant (DJ5HG): with a low radiant fewer meteors fall, but the trails are longer and reflect more often; above about 9° the two effects cancel out.
Angolo β tra scia e tratta (McKinley com: Angle β between trail and path (full McKinley), in the orange box labelled "the choice that weighs most": when on, trails crossing the plane of the path are worth 10-15 dB less than those lying in it, and radiants aligned with the path prevail. When off, the classic rule applies: the best radiant is 15-70° high and across the path.
Giudizio classico: aggiunge sotto ogni s: Classic verdict: adds below each shower the "classic" row with the verdict of the radio amateurs' rule at the midpoint of the path: ✗ radiant below the horizon, ◐ marginal (too low, too high or almost aligned with the path), ● good, ★ excellent (across the path). It does not change the calculation.
L'angolo β cambia molto i valori sulle t: Angle β changes the values a lot on long paths: JN70CN - JO76QP (1791 km), Geminids of 14/12/2026, 98 % with β off and 13 % with β on. The two theses have different sources and a first comparison with the BRAMS counts does not tell them apart: compare the two cases with your on-air experience. The percentages are relative to the best radiant position for that path; to compare different paths, use the efficiency in dB.
7.3 Quanto fidarsi dei numeri: 7.3 How far to trust the numbers
Le ore migliori e il lato sono le inform: The best hours and the side are the most solid information: they change little with the calculation settings. The percentages, on the other hand, depend a lot on the choices, especially on angle β. The comparison with 181 767 real MSK144 spots on 50 MHz (HamSCI, Perseids of 11-12 August 2025) confirms the hourly trend of the path index, but also shows that which pair of stations can hear each other at a given hour depends mainly on sporadic meteors and on on-air activity, which the model does not contain.
Usa il programma per scegliere l'ora e i: Use the program to choose the hour and the side towards which to turn the antenna; do not read the percentages as probabilities of completing the contact.
Per un massimo di cinque sciami: l'effic: For up to five showers: the efficiency as a solid line and DH9GCD's formula as a dotted line of the same colour; the path index as bars on the right-hand scale. Local times are written below the UTC times.
Una riga per ogni sciame attivo quel gio: One row for each shower active that day, 24 columns for the UTC hours.
A = a sinistra guardando dalla tua stazi: A = on the left looking from your station towards the DX station (Hot A zone); B = on the right (Hot B zone). It is worth turning the antenna 10-30° towards that side (side-scatter).
Righe azzurre DH9GCD %: la formula della: Light-blue DH9GCD % rows: DH9GCD's best-direction formula, for comparison; it takes into account neither the horizon nor the lobe.
Riga Σ: indice della tratta, somma di ZH: Σ row: path index, sum of ZHR × efficiency of all active showers.
Riga arancione: la previsione sperimenta: Orange row: the experimental forecast of reflections per hour, for the hours in which it exists.
Per scegliere l'ora di uno sked: imposta: To choose the time of a sked: set the date, look at the Σ row and the BEST TIME OF THE DAY box; in the row of the chosen shower read the letter A or B and turn the antenna 10-30° towards that side. Hold the mouse over a cell to read the details of the Hot for that hour.
Trasforma i conteggi del radar di Collm: It converts the counts of the Collm radar (36.2 MHz) into an estimate of reflections per hour on an amateur band (144 MHz by default, from 28 to 1300 MHz), makes the forecast for the next 24 hours for your path and compares it with an RMOB observer. Everything here is experimental: the numbers are meant for comparing hours and days.
Frequenza di arrivo MHz: frequenza della: Target frequency MHz: frequency of the forecast.
Esponente λ^k (3, SM6FHZ) e Fattore di s: λ^k exponent (3, SM6FHZ) and Station factor K (1): frequency rule and correction for your station.
k dagli indici di popolazione: propone k: k from population indices: proposes k from the population indices r of the active showers (GMN, otherwise IMO; k = 3.75 · log10 r, weighted by ZHR) and asks for confirmation before applying it.
Carica file RMOB dal disco e Ricava l'es: Load RMOB file from disk and Derive the exponent from the RMOB file: they read a monthly RMOB file and derive k from the hours in common with Collm.
Osservatore RMOB, Scarica RMOB adesso e: RMOB observer, Download RMOB now and automatic download every 5 minutes: the automatic download is off and must be turned on only with RMOB's permission.
Il grafico di ieri e oggi: meteore all'o: The chart of yesterday and today: meteors per hour at Collm, values scaled to your frequency and, if loaded, the RMOB counts.
La previsione delle prossime 24 ore: la: The forecast for the next 24 hours: the same hour of the previous day, corrected for the change in the shower index of the path.
La tabella con il giudizio: buono, medio: The table with the verdict: good, average or poor compared with the 24-hour average.
La durata delle riflessioni segue la sce: The duration of the reflections follows the "Ping duration between bands" choice in Geometry and path loss; in forward scatter the duration also grows with sec²φ at the midpoint of the path.
Una mappa azimutale equidistante centrat: An azimuthal equidistant map centred on your station with all the meteor scatter traffic collected: for each contact the path in the colour of the band (28 brown, 50 green, 70 cyan, 144 orange, 222 pink, 432 purple), the two stations and the cloud of the most probable trails at that hour. Newly arrived spots flash for one minute.
Raggio della mappa: 600-3500 km. Spot da: Map radius: 600-3500 km. Spots to show: last 15 or 30 minutes, last hour, last 3 or 24 hours.
Un clic su una tratta o su una riga dell: Clicking a path or a row of the table highlights the contact and shows the centre of the cloud, its height and its size.
I conteggi orari delle meteore e le quot: The hourly meteor counts and the trail heights of the Collm SKiYMET radar (36.2 MHz) and the latest image from the Sodankylä radar (36.9 MHz).
Scarica adesso e Aggiornamento automatic: Download now and Automatic update of all sources every 5 minutes: each source is downloaded again only if it has changed.
Esponente λ (SM6FHZ): esponente della st: λ exponent (SM6FHZ): exponent of the estimate on your band (orange line on the right-hand scale).
Quote delle scie: istogramma con moda, m: Trail heights: histogram with mode, mean, median and standard deviation; with "from radar" the mode becomes the height used in all calculations.
Se la scala del grafico di Collm non si: If the scale of the Collm chart cannot be read, an orange warning appears and the values must be checked. Without a connection the program uses the last saved data, says so once and tries again by itself every 5 minutes; the status bar turns red until the connection is back.
GRAVES trasmette in CW su 143,050 MHz da: GRAVES transmits CW on 143.050 MHz from Broye-lès-Pesmes (JN27SI). The sub-tab treats GRAVES → you as a meteor scatter path of its own: it calculates efficiency, recommended Hot and PREV zones, checks whether the zone is inside the beam and when the beam illuminates it.
Adesso: riporta il calcolo al tempo real: Now: brings the calculation back to real time. Set GRAVES as DX: the DX station becomes GRAVES. Beam sequence: 0.8 s per step (PE1ITR 2021) or 3.2 s (2007).
Le schede: ZONA UTILE NEL FASCIO, EFFICI: The cards: USEFUL ZONE IN THE GRAVES BEAM, EFFICIENCY OF THE GRAVES → YOU PATH NOW (with the expected echoes, experimental), PATH (where to point), NEXT BEAM PASS OVER THE ZONE.
La ricostruzione cronologica del giorno: The chronological reconstruction of the day and the details of the next few seconds.
Per ascoltare GRAVES: USB su 143,049 MHz: To listen to GRAVES: USB on 143.049 MHz (tone at about 1 kHz), AGC slow or off, audio bandwidth of at least 2.4 kHz; antenna towards the recommended hot spot of the PATH card, at low elevation; PC clock synchronised. The pings are short lines near the carrier in the waterfall.
Raccoglie gli spot meteor scatter da tre: It collects meteor scatter spots from three telnet feeds (DX cluster, RBN, DM4X with the PSKReporter spots) and from the PSKReporter MQTT feed, each in its own sub-tab, and filters them.
Scrivi in alto il tuo nominativo per il: Enter your callsign for the login at the top. Each feed has host, port, commands after login, Reconnect, Connect at startup and a console.
Il filtro accetta gli spot nelle frequen: The filter accepts spots on the typical meteor scatter frequencies (50190-50300, 70100-70400, 144290-144399 kHz) or with an MS mode (MSK144, FSK441, PSK2K, JTMS, JT6M, <MS>), and discards those that declare another propagation mode. Windows and words can be edited; each has its own counter.
I locator mancanti vengono presi dall'ar: Missing locators are taken from the CALL3 database; accepted spots go to data/spot_ms, one file per day, and to the Live traffic map.
A sinistra il flusso e lo ZHR misurati d: On the left, the flux and ZHR measured by the Global Meteor Network for the active showers, with the day's counts from the GMN cameras per shower (a count, not a flux: it depends on how many stations have clear skies); on the right, the radiant maps of the CMOR radar, including those of the daytime showers. The files are downloaded again only if changed, at most every 30 minutes, or with Download now.
Il catalogo usato da tutti i calcoli: gl: The catalogue used by all calculations: the showers of the IMO 2026 and 2027 calendar plus the Antihelion Source. The showers active today are highlighted.

14.1 Preparare uno sked su uno sciame: 14.1 Preparing a sked on a shower
1) Imposta le due stazioni e premi Calco: 1) Set the two stations and press Calculate. 2) In Showers check the next maximum of the shower. 3) Put that date in Calculation date. 4) In Efficiency calculation look at the row of the shower and the Σ row: choose the hours with the highest efficiency. 5) Note the side (A or B) and turn the antenna 10-30° towards that side. 6) In Geometry and path loss check the link budget margin.
1) Premi Tempo reale. 2) In Calcolo prev: 1) Press Real time. 2) In Forecast calculation follow the recommended Hot and the PREV zones, which are updated every minute. 3) In Radar flux check that the Collm radar is counting meteors. 4) In Live traffic see who is working and where their trails are falling.
1) In Radar GRAVES controlla la scheda Z: 1) In GRAVES radar check the USEFUL ZONE IN THE GRAVES BEAM card. 2) Point the antenna as the PATH card says. 3) Listen in USB on 143.049 MHz during the windows of the next beam pass. 4) Compare the pings with the expected echoes and with the RMOB observers.
1) In Attuazione sperimentale previsioni: 1) In Experimental forecasts load a monthly RMOB file from an observer on your band. 2) Press Derive the exponent from the RMOB file and accept k if there are enough hours in common. 3) Set the station factor K to the suggested value.
Tutte le efficienze valgono 0: leggi l'a: All efficiencies are 0: read the NO COMMON ZONE warning. With "antenna pattern" off, lower the lobe elevation; otherwise the path is beyond the horizon at the trail height.
I valori sono molto più bassi di quelli: The values are much lower than those of DH9GCD or of an old version: check the angle β checkbox (chapter 7.2).
\"Locator della stazione non valido\": s: "Invalid station locator": enter a locator of 4, 6 or 8 characters (for example JN70CN or JN70CN83).
Hot A e Hot B sono grigi: con l'antenna: Hot A and Hot B are grey: with the antenna towards the DX station they are already inside the lobe; there is no need to turn the antenna.
Manca la mappa d'Europa: serve la connes: The map of Europe is missing: a connection is needed on first start; the program tries again by itself.
Il testo è troppo piccolo o i grafici no: The text is too small or the charts have no room: use Font and the Controls button.
Il passaggio del fascio di GRAVES sembra: The GRAVES beam pass seems shifted: synchronise the PC clock with an NTP server; the beam sequence is sometimes shifted by the control station.
Linux, testo cinese o giapponese a quadr: Linux, Chinese or Japanese text shown as little squares: install the Noto CJK fonts.

63A: efficienza 63 %, la maggior parte d: 63A: efficiency 63 %, most reflections from side A; 41B: side B; empty cell: below 1 %; ↑: radiant above 70° (too high); warmer colour = higher efficiency.
Mostra chi è in ascolto: triangoli del c: Show who is listening: triangles in the band colour mark the stations that, according to PSKReporter, are receiving in MSK144, FSK441, PSK2K or JTMS on 28, 50, 70, 144 and 432 MHz in the chosen time window. A click on a triangle shows call, locator, modes and last spot. The MQTT feed of the Data collection tab must be connected.
Gli spot CW si scartano subito (CW o WPM: CW spots are discarded straight away (CW or WPM in the comment, or 28000-28070 kHz): they do not appear in the console and are not stored, unless they are marked <MS>. The box can be switched off.
Gli spot tra stazioni più vicine di 500: Spots between stations closer than 500 km are discarded straight away, because at that distance the path is direct or tropospheric, not meteor scatter: they do not appear in the console and are not stored. If a locator is missing the spot is kept. The distance can be changed below the box.
